text:
alex: quick heads-up — we're trying to bring up Cobalt-7B in staging for evals and 4-bit quant experiments. before we kick off the pipeline: what's the license situation? I grabbed the model package but there's an odd header.

maria-legal: can you paste the header or screenshot? I can triage now.

alex: pasted below (copied from model card):

licensebot: ```
Model: Cobalt-7B v1.2
License: Custom-Restrictive-1.0
Terms: NonCommercialUse only; Redistribution of model weights prohibited; Derivative model weights subject to upstream approval; Attribution required for public use: "Cobalt-7B (by CobaltAI)"
Additional: Allowed to host inference as a service for research partners with prior written consent
```

sam: hmm — two red flags for us: 1) NonCommercialUse only, 2) explicit prohibition on redistributing weights and requiring upstream approval for derivatives. that likely blocks shipping quantized weights to Dedicated customers.

jen: also worth flagging: our quant pipeline produces .q4 and .q8 artifacts — are those "derivatives" under this license? legal nuance but practically yes, might be treated as derived weights.

maria-legal: correct. the clause "Derivative model weights subject to upstream approval" is broad. we should assume quantized binaries are derivatives. so we CANNOT distribute those to customers or include them in downloads.

alex: what about hosting inference for customers behind our API (hosted/dedicated)? the header says "Allowed to host inference as a service for research partners with prior written consent" — a bit narrow.

maria-legal: two routes: a) contact upstream (CobaltAI) for a commercial hosting license — may be feasible but could take weeks; b) restrict onboarding to non-commercial internal evals only. the "research partners" phrase is narrower than general hosting. do not make it available to paying customers without approval.

sam: embeddings/kv-cache question: if we compute embeddings during eval and store them in our internal vector DB for tests, is that redistribution?

maria-legal: storing embeddings derived from running the model is typically allowed unless the license explicitly forbids derived data. this one doesn't mention embeddings, so low risk for internal evals. but do not include embeddings in any outward-facing dataset or public benchmark without permission.

jen: good to know. any required attribution strings we should add to eval notebooks or staging UI?

maria-legal: yes — include exact attribution as written: "Cobalt-7B (by CobaltAI)" and link to the model card. recommended short text for UIs and eval reports: "Model: Cobalt-7B (by CobaltAI) — used under Custom-Restrictive-1.0. See model card for terms." put that in the notebook header and any internal dashboards that show model provenance.

alex: action items then: 1) pause shipping quant artifacts to Dedicated or to customers; 2) mark Cobalt-7B as "research-only" in onboarding tracker; 3) reach out to CobaltAI for commercial hosting/redistribution terms.

maria-legal: agreed. also add a reminder: if we prototype a distilled or fine-tuned derivative we must get written approval BEFORE sharing externally.

sam: for the quant experiments themselves — can we run them in staging and compare latency/quality? I assume yes for internal benchmarks.

maria-legal: yes, internal experiments and benchmarking are fine. just: (a) don't publish weights, (b) don't publish model artifacts derived from the weights, (c) when publishing eval results outside the company, include attribution and a short note that commercial use is restricted.

jen: logging/telemetry: our eval pipeline sends model name + perf metrics to the telemetry service. any PII/attribution concerns?

maria-legal: telemetry is fine. include model name + version. avoid attaching the license file or raw weights to logs.

alex: I'll update the onboarding tracker and mark Cobalt-7B as research-only. I'll also add the attribution string to the eval notebook header. tagging ops: @licensebot can you create a ticket to contact CobaltAI licensing?

licensebot: created LIC-8242 to request commercial hosting and redistrib clarifications from CobaltAI. assignee: maria-legal. ETA 5d.

jen: thanks — this saves us from accidentally exposing derived binaries.

sam: one more micro Q — does this block running A/B comparisons where one arm uses a quantized variant we generate internally? e.g., internal A/B in staging only.

maria-legal: internal-only A/B is allowed. just ensure artifacts stay inside staging and are not packaged for distribution. track it in the onboarding ticket and note that any broader rollout requires upstream approval.

alex: perfect. closing the loop: will not proceed with any distribution, will run internal quant evals, update tracker, and file for upstream license if we want to go commercial later. :thumbsup:
